page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m1.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine instance within the ecs.m1 family. It is built on the x86_64 CPU architecture and features 4 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor and does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

This instance type does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through network-attached block storage. It also lacks dedicated GPU hardware, with a GPU count of zero. Furthermore, the CPU configuration lacks support for advanced instruction sets and hardware-accelerated features, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), cryptographic acceleration (AES, SHA_NI), and hardware virtualization extensions (VMX, SVM).

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.m1.medium offers stable compute performance for standard workloads. However, the absence of modern vector and cryptographic instruction sets makes it less efficient for tasks requiring heavy mathematical computation, machine learning inference, or high-throughput encryption. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as basic web serving, lightweight application servers, and development environments that do not rely on specialized CPU instructions or local disk performance.
